title: Tesserae plugin manifest
description: Shape of plugin.json. See docs/contracts/plugins.md for the prose contract.

tesserae_compat.description: Major version range this plugin works against (e.g. '1.x'). The loader rejects mismatches.

admin_title.description: What the Widgets menu's Admin pages list and the admin page itself call the plugin's admin page, when that should differ from name (e.g. 'Newspapers' for 'News, Front Pages'). Defaults to name.

category.description: Subject the editor's widget picker groups this widget under. Optional; without it the picker guesses from the family in the name and falls back to utility.

fragments.description: Named, independently-placeable pieces of the widget for the Panels canvas editor. render() paints just one when it receives ctx.fragment; a widget with no fragments (or ctx.fragment absent) renders the whole widget. Declaring fragments lets a user drop, say, just the temperature or the sun-times of a weather widget onto the canvas. See docs/dev/writing-a-widget.md.

id.description: Fragment id passed to render() as ctx.fragment. 'full' is reserved for the whole widget.

secret.description: The value is sensitive: it is stripped from the render context handed to the browser and redacted (with an installer question suggested in its place) when the dashboard is shared to the catalog.

mask.description: Render the editor field as a password input. Defaults to the value of 'secret'. Set false on a sensitive value the author still has to be able to read to maintain, such as a URL.

image.description: A picture of the choice (a path on this server such as /plugins/<id>/static/x.jpg, or an https URL). When any choice of a select has one, the editor shows a picture picker instead of a plain dropdown.

image_large.description: A bigger copy of image, shown when the picker's picture is enlarged. Defaults to image.

presets.description: For a textarea: an Examples dropdown above it; picking one fills the textarea with the preset's value, to be edited from there.

fill_from.description: Another option owns this field's value; the editor fills it and locks it. Resolved server-side, so the field updates on reload after a save rather than the instant the controlling option changes. See docs/widgets.md.

option.description: Name of the controlling cell option.

map.description: Controlling value -> value for this field.

show_if.description: Show this field only when other options match. Keys are option names, every key must match. A value is an exact match, a list is any-of, and {"not": value-or-list} is none-of. A field whose controlling option is hidden is hidden too. Hidden fields keep their value. See docs/widgets.md.

advanced.description: Fine-tuning a typical user never needs to touch (refresh interval, title, text size, typeface, sort order and the like). Tesserae renders these last, in manifest order, inside a collapsed "More options" section at the end of the options form. show_if still applies inside it. An older Tesserae ignores the key and shows the option as usual. See docs/widgets.md.

secret.description: When true, this field is saved to settings.json as '<name>_secret' so disk-grepping reveals which values are sensitive.

advanced.description: As on cell_options: render this setting last, inside the collapsed "More options" section of the widget's settings card.

then.description: A repeater: a list of rows, each with the sub-fields in 'fields', added, removed and reordered in the settings card. Stored as a JSON list of objects keyed by sub-field name. See docs/widgets.md.

type.description: No nesting: a repeater can't hold another repeater.

required.description: A row can't be saved with this blank.

unique.description: string or select: no two rows may share a value (compared ignoring case and surrounding spaces).

max_length.description: string or textarea; defaults to 500 and 5000.

pattern.description: string only: what the whole (trimmed) value must look like, in a small regex subset matched without backtracking: literal characters, . and [classes] (ranges, ^, \d, \w), each with an optional count (* + ? {n} {n,} {n,m}), at most one part varying in length, no groups, alternation or anchors. Inside a class write a literal - or / as \- and \/.

format.description: string only: "url" takes only an http(s) address with a host (or nothing).

pattern_hint.description: What the pattern asks for, in words, shown when a value doesn't match.

monospace.description: textarea: a fixed-width font, for code.

add_label.description: The add button's text. Defaults to "Add row".

row_label.description: What one row is called, for screen readers ("Paper 2 of 4"). Defaults to "Row".

list.description: How an admin page drawing this repeater as a list (repeater_layout="list") shows its rows: title (sub-field names tried in turn for the row title), summary (a sub-field shown beside it), fixed ({sub-field: [values]}: rows that can't be removed) and add (false drops the Add button). See app/repeater.py list_options.

data_schema.description: Declares the widget's fetch() data shape so the Panels canvas editor can offer its fields as bindable data sources. Optional: a widget without this block still renders normally but has no bindable fields in the composer. See docs/dev/writing-a-widget.md.

color.description: Optional accent colour for the widget's card in the composer Data panel.

fields.description: The bindable fields, one per top-level fetch() result key worth exposing.

type.description: num (number), str (text/state), or arr (list, e.g. a series or item list).

label.description: Human-friendly field name shown in the bind list.

sample.description: Representative values keyed by field name, matching fetch()'s shape. Powers the editor's live preview and the render fallback when a source isn't configured yet.

per_placement.description: Fetch data separately for each canvas placement and its dimensions instead of sharing by plugin and options.

updates.description: Declares host-owned update triggers this widget supports. A declaration only makes the matching per-placement opt-in available; it never refreshes a dashboard by itself.

on_change.description: Data sources that may refresh an opted-in placement. selector_option optionally narrows an event to the placement's selected cell option value.

source.description: Stable server data-change source id, for example personal_data.reminders.

selector_option.description: Optional cell_options name whose saved value narrows the dependency, for example list_id.

on_schedule.description: Scheduled refresh kinds supported by this widget. suggested_at only prefills the optional custom-time control; omitting a placement time means the local day boundary.

suggested_at.description: Optional HH:MM prefill for a user-selected custom time.

design.description: Design-system intent. Default for every field is the strict, palette-safe behaviour; opt-in values signal a widget is using a richer surface and accepts the downstream trade-offs.

palette.description: `strict` (default): the widget only uses Spectra colour tokens (`--w-orange`, `--w-blue`, etc.), so the rendered output lands cleanly on every supported panel without dithering. `extended`: the widget uses arbitrary CSS colours and relies on the renderer's Floyd-Steinberg pass to approximate them on the panel palette. Good for scenic/decorative widgets (gradients, soft scenery); read worse on BW panels than strict widgets. Catalog reviewers should see this flag and treat extended widgets as taking on the dither-tradeoff responsibility.

requires.description: Declared capability list. Each entry is `<category>:<value>`. Supported categories: `network:<hostname>` (specific egress target; `network:*` for unrestricted but flagged in review), `settings:plugin` (own plugin settings, the common case; `settings:plugin/<other_id>` for a sibling's; `settings:app` for top-level app settings like lat/lon), `filesystem:write:<path>` (write outside data_dir; reads are implicit for data_dir and the plugin folder), `plugin:<other_id>` (this widget fetches through another plugin, so that plugin's declared hosts are allowed while this one runs; needed because the delegate's request happens inside this widget's capability scope). Enforcement in v1: network egress is blocked at the socket layer for hostnames not in the list; settings + filesystem entries are review-only. Widgets without a `requires:` block load with no enforcement (existing behaviour) but should declare in new submissions, the catalog review checklist demands it.

locales.description: locale tags this widget ships panel text for (e.g. 'en', 'fr', 'pt-BR'). Each tag must have a matching strings/<tag>.json file next to plugin.json, a flat { "key": "translated text" } map. A widget's own hardcoded fallback text is always assumed to be English; strings/en.json is what a locale with no exact or base-language match falls back to. The host resolves the active locale (per device, falling back to the app default) and hands the widget ctx.locale + ctx.strings/ctx.t() at render time. See docs/widgets.md#locales-strings.

allOf.description: Placeable widgets must declare at least one size; non-placeable kinds (service, data, font, admin) may leave supports.sizes empty.
Only placeable widgets may declare update capabilities.
Only placeable widgets render panel text, so only they may declare locales.
